subject: Post-call: Pricing & batching discussion with Acme - next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - Pricing, token volumes, batching

Hi John / Sara,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning - good conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned:

Summary of requirements we discussed:
- Primary use case: in-product assistance (search + short completions) and some scheduled batch jobs for summarization.
- Traffic profile: many small interactive requests with occasional larger background jobs.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for interactive flows.

Customer-ish numbers you shared:
- Expected monthly token consumption (initial): 50M - 200M tokens/month (growth expected over 6-12 months).
- Typical request size (avg): ~100 tokens (30 token prompt + 70 token completion).
- Peak concurrency: bursts up to ~60-80 rps; steady-state interactive 5-20 rps depending on day.
- Budget range: roughly $8k - $30k/month allocated for inference initially.

Unit economics and target: (from your side) target unit cost around $150 per 1M tokens (acceptable range $100-$250/1M). We flagged that continuous batching and caching are the lever we expect to use to get closer to the low end of that range.

Batching & concurrency assumptions we agreed to validate in the POC:
- Continuous batching is likely to be effective because the workload is mostly many small requests with sustained traffic windows.
- Assumed average batch yield: 8-16 requests per kernel call in steady-state (varies by region/time).
- Expected effective throughput improvement from continuous batching: 2-3x compared to naive single-request execution (depends on model size & latency SLO).
- Concurrency profile to simulate: baseline 20 rps sustained, spikes to 80 rps for 2-10 minute windows.

Next steps (action items):
- I'll send a short pricing sketch + assumptions spreadsheet (attached) that shows cost under three scenarios (hosted, committed Dedicated, Dedicated + caching). -> see attachment: batching-assumptions.xlsx
- Aditya will follow up with a suggested POC plan (technical integration + sample dataset + duration).
- John / Sara: confirm whether we should include SOC 2 evidence and an NDA prior to the POC.

Attachments: Redwood_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal), batching-assumptions.xlsx (assumptions + sample cost calc).

If that matches your memory, we'll put together a one-page commitment estimate and a proposed POC timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - Pricing, token volumes, batching

John -

Good questions. Quick pricing sketch here to make the apples-to-apples comparison:

Assumptions (for the draft calc in batching-assumptions.xlsx):
- Tokens counted = prompt + completion. We modeled avg request = 100 tokens total.
- Monthly tokens scenarios: 50M / 100M / 200M.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for interactive route.
- Continuous batching yield (observed in similar customers): 2.5x effective throughput improvement (range 2.0-3.0x) vs naive single-request.
- Effective model/infra unit cost baseline (hosted open model estimate): $350 per 1M tokens before batching/compression. This number bundles model runtime and infra without committed discounts.

Sample unit economics (post-batching & discounts):
- Hosted (no commit): modeled baseline $350/1M -> with continuous batching assume 2.5x improvement -> effective $140/1M tokens.
- Committed Dedicated (1yr commit + autoscale + caching): baseline infra discounts and KV caching -> modeled $90-120/1M tokens depending on commit level and cache hit rate.
- Target you mentioned ($150/1M) is achievable in Hosted for steady workloads via continuous batching; Dedicated gets you below $120/1M in most consistent patterns.

Examples (rounded):
- 50M tokens/month: Hosted est ~ $7k/month; Dedicated est (committed) ~ $4.5k/month.
- 200M tokens/month: Hosted est ~ $28k/month; Dedicated est ~ $18k/month.

Key levers to hit lower $/1M: batching yield (higher is better), prefix/KV cache hit rate (for repeated prompts), and commit level for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools). Our POC will instrument these and produce a per-route cost breakdown.

I attached the spreadsheet with the line-by-line math: batching-assumptions.xlsx.

If that looks aligned I'll propose a short 2-week technical POC:
- Week 0: keys + small integration + traffic shaping to match production profile
- Week 1: run sustained traffic (20 rps baseline, 80 rps spikes) and capture batching metrics + p95 latency
- Week 2: optimize batching/caching config, produce final cost report and recommended commit level

Camila / Marissa: can you confirm the POC timeline and whether Acme needs an NDA first?

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
